facts.statement: Enigmosaurus is a genus of therizinosauroid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Enigmosaurus (meaning "enigma lizard" or "enigmatic lizard") is a genus of therizinosauroid that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The name Enigmosaurus means "enigma lizard" and refers to the unusual shape of its pelvis.
facts.quote: The generic name, Enigmosaurus, was stated to be derived from Greek (aínigma, meaning enigma) and (sauros, meaning lizard), in reference to the aberratic and unusual shape of its pelvis.

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull but including a well-preserved pelvic girdle and other postcranial bones.
facts.quote: The preserved elements consist of a partial skeleton, lacking the skull, that includes a well preserved pelvic girdle with other postcrania.

facts.statement: Enigmosaurus was estimated to reach a length of 5 meters and a weight between 454 and 907 kilograms.
facts.quote: Enigmosaurus was a relatively large-bodied therizinosaur, with an estimated length of 5 m and a weight between 454 and 907 kg.

facts.statement: The holotype pelvis preserves the sacral vertebrae, partial ilium, both pubis bones, and the left ischium.
facts.quote: The holotype pelvis is in relatively good preservation, compromising the sacral vertebrae, partial ilium, right and left pubis and the left ischium.

facts.statement: The pelvis of Enigmosaurus is described as large and opisthopubic.
facts.quote: The pelvis is somewhat large as a whole and opisthopubic.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Enigmosaurus preserves six vertebrae with elongated transverse processes.
facts.quote: Apparently, the sacrum preserves six vertebrae, with elongated transverse processes.

facts.statement: Enigmosaurus lived between approximately 95.9 and 89.6 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Santonian ages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The remains of Enigmosaurus were found in sediments that were deposited during the Late Cretaceous period on the Bayan Shireh Formation, Khara Khutul locality, about 95.9 ± 6.0 million to 89.6 ± 4.0 million years ago, Cenomanian–Santonian ages.

facts.statement: Most authors suggest that Enigmosaurus was likely a slow herbivore or omnivore.
facts.quote: Being a therizinosaur, it was likely a slow herbivore and/or omnivore, as suggested by most authors all over the time.

facts.statement: Enigmosaurus was originally placed in the obsolete family Enigmosauridae but is now classified within the Therizinosauridae.
facts.quote: Enigmosaurus was by the describers assigned to a separate Enigmosauridae (now obsolete) due to its aberrant pelvis, but later considered a member of the Segnosauridae which are today called the Therizinosauridae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the unique pelvic traits of Enigmosaurus are due to the animal's advanced age rather than being unique species characteristics, requiring further analysis.
facts.quote: These specific traits may indicate the advanced age of the individual; if true, the fusion of the obturator process and pubic body could be discarded as an authentic autapomorphy for the species. Zanno noted that more analyses are required to settle this enigma.

facts.statement: Enigmosaurus was nicknamed the "Dinosaur from Khara Khutul" due to the location where its fossils were found.
facts.quote: Nicknamed as the "Dinosaur from Khara Khutul", it was shortly described and included into the Segnosauria.

facts.statement: Fossils of Enigmosaurus were discovered in 1980 in the Baynshirenskaya Svita formation near Khar Hötöl, Mongolia.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles del Enigmosaurus fueron descubiertos en 1980 en Baynshirenskaya Svita, Khar Hötöl, Mongolia

facts.statement: The fossils were initially described as an indeterminate dinosaur close to Segnosauria and formally named in 1983.
facts.quote: siendo descritos e ilustrados como un dinosaurio indeterminado cercano al Segnosaurio y nombrado, posteriormente, en 1983

facts.statement: The generic name Enigmosaurus comes from the Greek word for 'enigma' due to the confusing and unusual shape of its pelvis.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego αἴνιγμα, ainigma, "enigma", después de la forma desconcertante e inusual de su pelvis

facts.statement: The type species Enigmosaurus mongoliensis is known only from the holotype IGM 100/84, consisting of an incomplete ischium and pelvis.
facts.quote: La especie tipo Enigmosaurus mongoliensis se conoce solamente por el holotipo, IGM 100/84, un isquion y una pelvis incompletos

facts.statement: The holotype is about 95% the size of the Segnosaurus holotype, leading to a tentative estimate that the animal measured 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: que es el cerca del 95% del tamaño del holotipo de Segnosaurus. Esto lleva a una estimación tentativa de que media 5 metros de largo

facts.statement: No more than six sacral vertebrae were present, featuring elongated sacral ribs.
facts.quote: No más de seis vértebras sacras estaban presentes, con las costillas sacras alargadas

facts.statement: The pubic peduncle is thicker and projects more ventrally than in Segnosaurus or Nanshiungosaurus, a trait shared with Alxasaurus.
facts.quote: El pedúnculo púbico es más grueso y proyectado más a ventral que Segnosaurus o Nanshiungosaurus, como en Alxasaurus

facts.statement: The puboischiac foramen is larger than in Segnosaurus or Nanshiungosaurus.
facts.quote: Hay una ventana puboisquial más grande que Segnosaurus o Nanshiungosaurus

facts.statement: Barsbold and Perle proposed the genus as part of Segnosauria but separated it from Segnosaurus and Erlikosaurus into the distinct family Enigmosauridae.
facts.quote: Barsbold y Perle propusieron a este género como parte de Segnosauria, pero la separaron de Segnosaurus y de Erlikosaurus en una familia separada el Enigmosauridae

facts.statement: Enigmosaurus is currently classified within the group Therizinosauria.
facts.quote: Actualmente se lo incluye en Therizinosauria

facts.statement: It is considered more advanced than Beipiaosaurus and appears to have a reduced postacetabular process compared to Alxasaurus, placing it in the family Therizinosauroidea.
facts.quote: Es más avanzado que Beipiaosaurus y parecería tener un proceso postacetabular más reducido que Alxasaurus, por lo que se incluye en la familia Therizinosauroidea

facts.statement: The parent group for Enigmosaurus is Therizinosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Therizinosauridae

facts.statement: Enigmosaurus lived during the Cenomanian to Santonian stages, approximately 100.5 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Santonian (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether some elements from the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian Iren Dabasu Formation belong to Enigmosaurus, though they are more likely to be Erliansaurus or Neimongosaurus.
facts.quote: Se ha sugerido que algunos elementos de la Formación Iren Dabasu del último Campaniense, Maastrichtiense temprano puedan ser referibles a Enigmosaurus, pero es más probable que sean Erliansaurus o Neimongosaurus

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether Enigmosaurus might actually be the pelvis of Erlikosaurus, arguing that Segnosaurus and Erlikosaurus are too similar to have such distinct pelvic structures.
facts.quote: Enigmosaurus podría ser la pelvis de Erlikosaurus, que es desconocida, pero Barsbold y Perle propusieron que Segnosaurus y Erlikosaurus eran demasiado similares para tener pelvis tan distintas
